analysis.investment_thesis: Black Box scores well on return on capital (~33% ROIC, ROCE 29.8%) but fails the Magic Formula's equally critical earnings yield test at just ~5.2% EBIT/EV — well below the 12% minimum threshold for attractiveness. The business is a good one priced too richly to act on.
key_strengths: High ROIC ~33% (EBIT INR 538 Cr / Invested Capital ~INR 1,633 Cr) — sustained capital efficiency
Operating income CAGR of 64.8% over 9 years, with a clear expanding trend in FY24–25
key_risks: Earnings yield only ~5.2% (EV ~INR 10,335 Cr vs EBIT INR 538 Cr) — well below Magic Formula's 12% floor
FCF turned sharply negative in FY25 (-INR 129 Cr) and OCF also negative (-INR 88 Cr) — working capital deterioration
Debt rising fast (INR 628 Cr → INR 942 Cr in 2 years) while revenue actually contracted YoY (INR 6,282 → INR 5,967 Cr)
red_flags: Negative Free Cash Flow in FY25 (-INR 129 Cr) undermines the quality of reported EBIT
Finance costs INR 145 Cr = 27% of EBIT — interest burden severely clips equity returns
Other income persistently negative (FY25: -INR 68 Cr), suggesting recurring forex or goodwill charges obscured in EBIT
Revenue declining YoY in FY25 contradicts the growth premium embedded in 35x P/E
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict: Black Box passes the quality screen (ROIC ~33%, ROCE 29.8%) but fails the value screen decisively. EV ≈ INR 10,335 Cr (Market Cap INR 9,607 Cr + Debt INR 942 Cr − Cash INR 214 Cr) against EBIT of INR 538 Cr yields an earnings yield of only 5.2% — less than half the 12% Greenblatt threshold. At P/E 35x and EV/EBITDA 21.7x, the market is paying a steep multiple for thin 7.3% operating margins in a largely systems-integration/IT-services business with significant debt (D/E 1.15). The Magic Formula only rewards companies cheap enough that even modest execution delivers strong returns; at current prices, there's no margin of safety.

Operational quality is a mixed picture. The 9-year EBIT CAGR of 64.8% is impressive but heavily driven by the 2019 acquisition (revenue jumped from INR 733 Cr to INR 1,853 Cr then INR 4,994 Cr). More worryingly, FY25 OCF turned negative (-INR 88 Cr) for the first time since the consolidation, borrowings jumped INR 230 Cr in one year, and revenue contracted. Finance costs of INR 145 Cr consume 27% of EBIT, meaning reported ROE (44%) is heavily leveraged and fragile. This is a decent business at a bad price — watch for earnings yield to improve to 10%+ (EV compression or EBIT doubling) before revisiting.
